topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture on complement and frames its importance and nomenclature challenges.

topics.label: Overview, nomenclature, and central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: They establish the general architecture, naming conventions, and central C3 cleavage mechanism of the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: They explain the mechanisms of the alternative, lectin, and classical pathways that drive complement deposition and reach the activation threshold.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the downstream processes through which activated complement mediates opsonization, inflammation, and direct cell lysis.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: It details the regulatory proteins and inhibitory mechanisms that protect healthy host cells from complement-mediated damage.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It examines the distinct disease patterns and clinical vulnerabilities caused by deficiencies in individual complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: It details the strategies evolved by pathogens, exemplified by Staphylococcus aureus, to circumvent complement attack.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the discussion on complement and previews the upcoming lecture on adaptive immunity.
